text:
maria: Noticed a sharp uptick in host CPU on the streaming ingress hosts starting ~10:17 UTC. Tail latency for some customers spiked. Profiling shows writev/syscall hotpath and lots of tiny frames.

joel: Any traces? sounds like many small frames hitting writev instead of a coalesced write. Could be a client change or header churn.

maria: Paste from perf top (sample window):
```
  28.6%  host-proxy       syscall_writev
  14.1%  host-preproc     parse_request_frag
  11.3%  runtime          kernel_picker_select
   9.7%  tokenizer        normalize_utf8
   6.5%  kv-store         handle_miss_alloc
```
strace showed ~5-10 writev calls per streamed message, average payload ~180 bytes.

tina: KV metrics show a +3.1% miss increase coincident with this window; that will amplify expensive parse cold-paths. We had a pod OOM event earlier that nudged eviction policy.

lucy: Two quick experiments I ran in staging: (A) bump gateway coalesce buffer from 128->512 bytes -> syscall count dropped 42%, tail latency down ~18ms; (B) force kernel_picker to prefer vectorized kernel for short sequences -> decode CPU down ~6% but no large tail impact.

joel: Interesting. That suggests IO amplification is the bigger lever. But kernel selection still matters for CPU-bound workloads. We should surface the upstream observed frame size as a signal to kernel_picker. If ingress coalesce is low, kernel_picker might prefer a conservative codepath since micro-batching will be small.

maria: Agreed. Proposed short-term changes: 1) increase default gateway coalesce to 512 bytes; 2) add an ingress micro-batch delay of 0.8ms configurable; 3) pin kv_cache capacity on canary nodes to previous level to rule out eviction churn; 4) add telemetry that records ingress_coalesce_bytes -> kernel_id mapping.

tina: I'll pin cache size on canary and revert eviction aggressiveness. Also will add alert if kv miss rate delta > 1% in 5m window.

lucy: I'll open PR to make coalesce default 512 and a flag --ingress-coalesce-bytes. Also adding a short jitter option --ingress-coalesce-delay-ms with default 0.0. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1234.

joel: I'll modify kernel_picker to record a histogram: observed_ingress_frame_size -> chosen_kernel and ship it to perf.metrics. We can then correlate kernel_id choices with coalesce sizes.

maria: Test plan: run wrk streaming script that simulates fragmented clients (script attach) across baseline and canary. Measure syscall rate, host CPU, 95th latency. Run on 3 node canary for 2h before wider rollout.

perf-bot: Perf job queued: nightly/edge-coalesce-experiment. Baseline run attached.

lucy: Rollout/rollback: roll to 10% -> 25% -> 100% if 95th tail improves or stays flat. Rollback if 95th tail increases by >10% or host-token CPU increases by >7% over 30m.

maria: Also ask clients team to check if they recently changed gRPC metadata usage (per-request unique headers) which would defeat HPACK reuse. If so, we should recommend reusing metadata or switch to header compression hints.

joel: I'll also run quick comparison between raw HTTP/2 streaming and HTTP/1.1 proxy path to quantify HPACK impact.

tina: I'll post KV eviction logs and pod memory events for the window.

maria: Thanks. Assigning owners: lucy (proxy PR), joel (kernel_picker telemetry), tina (kv pin + alerts). Will reconvene after canary runs. :thumbsup:
